newsitem.title: UKRAINE: RUSSIA '97 OIL EXPORT VIA UKRAINE SEEN AT 16MLN.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA '97 OIL EXPORT VIA UKRAINE SEEN AT 16MLN.

text.p: Russian oil supplies to Central and Eastern European customers in 1997 through the Ukrainian stretch of Druzhba pipeline seen at least at 16 million tonnes, energy official said on Thursday.
Stepan Yaloveha, spokesman for State Oil and Gas Committee said that such an amount is guaranteed but talks with Russian exporters still were going on.

"There will be both inter-state and commercial contracts but yearly amount of the transported oil will be at least 16 million tonnes despite that we could transport up to 20 million tonnes," Yaloveha told Reuters by telephone.

Flows via Ukraine's stretch of the Druzhba pipeline fell to 16.6 million tonnes in 1996 compared to 18 million tonnes in 1995. About 80 Russian energy firms supply oil via Druzhba to the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary and former Yugoslavia.

Druzhba's (Friendship) total capacity is about 60 million tonnes, which includes the Belarus stretch to Poland and Germany, has not been largerly used since the collapse of the former Soviet Union because many European clients were keen to diversify oil supplies or had no cash to pay.

Yaloveha said that Druzhba has been charging Russian suplliers $5.2 per tonne for the whole Ukrainian stretch despite several rounds of talks between Russian and Ukrainian energy officials last year produced no results.
